description.narrative:
Water Supply - 2000 households (12,000 people) will be provided with water on a daily basis through existing suppliers in the camps- Iftin, Gaduudey, Albarako, Shabeel, Wabari, Bula-cesan, Hawal-cadey- the water will be distributed for a period of one month i.e., 30 days. Each Household will receive a approximately 45 liters per day. SADO will ensure that the water from the suppliers is treated with chlorine and testing the water for contamination. At water source, water sample will be sampled and tested for bacterial (feacal coliform and total coliform) and chemical (pH, turbidity, hardness among others) to ensure water is safe for human consumption. The SADO WASH officers will continue to monitor the water quality. At household level, water will be treated using aqua tabs distributed among other items in the hygiene kit. Each household will receive 100 aqua tabs to be used for 3 months, based on the average volume of water per household of 45 liters per day in accordance with the Sphere Standards.
Hygiene promotion: SADO will identify hygiene promoters in Bardera districts in the targeted villages who will be trained on hygiene promotion activities and skills. 60% of these will be women and 40% men. Women will constitute a higher percentage of the hygiene promoters as they are the primary caregivers at domestic level and will therefore be able to reach other women and children. These hygiene promoters will be selected by the communities through the established Village Relief Committees as well asin consultation with SADO field teams. The aim of hygiene promotion is to promote behavioral change and good hygiene practices within the IDP camps. Their task will dissemination of IEC materials, water treatment at household level (aqua tabs)/safe waterstorage through cleaning of water containers, solid waste management (safe disposal of waste), conducting door to door hygiene campaigns and having key informant interviews with the beneficiaries and promoting hand washing with soap at critical moment (before eating, before cooking, after visiting the toilet, after changing babies nappies and before breastfeeding). Hygiene promoters will also promote the importance of using aqua-tabs and emphasize to beneficiary households the risks related to water-borne diseases. The aquatabs provided should be sufficient for three months use, assumingthat households use it at the rate of 45 liters of water treated per day (7.5 liters per household member with an average of 6 members per household). SADO will recommendfor the use of 1 aqua tab (167 mg) for 20 litres for households whose primary source of water is turbid while for households obtaining water from non-turbid sources 67mg aqua tabs will be distributed.

participating-org.narrative: Social Life and Agricultural Development Organization (SADO) is a Somalia based Local Non-Governmental Organization (LNGO) established in 1994 with the aim of spearheading local development initiatives in GEDO region and other parts of South-Central Somalia. SADOis legally registered in Kenya and in Somalia under Somalia Federal Government and in Jubaland State of Somalia. With its headquarters in Mogadishu, Somalia, SADO has base stations in Kismayu, Bardera, Elwak, Garbaharrey, Belt Hawa and Dollow Districts of Somalia. It has operational presence and experience in the greater Horn of Africa. SADO is a firm believer in the fundamental moral principle of humanity; that all human begins are born free and equal in dignity and rights and therefore action should be taken to prevent or alleviate human suffering arising out of disaster or conflict, and that nothing should override this principle. Our activities are grounded on the rights-based approach on the belief that people are entitled to basic conditions of living with dignity and have access to equal opportunity as a basis of fulfilling their human potential. MISSION Our mission is to work with our partners in improving the quality of life of vulnerable communities in Somalia through facilitating humanitarian aid and sustainable development programs. A horn of Africa in which vulnerable communities live in dignity and security. CORE VALUES SADO believes in, and is guided by the following ideals: respect, moral and ethical standards, making sound judgments in our programming and innovations.
